witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius A.iii (K1); but for the Quadripartitus and the London texts Liebermann’s K means Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 57.5
div.ab: Si quis in curia sua rectum de hominibus suis facturus sit, nominentur ei qui inplacitantur; et competenti termino satisfaccionem habeant; nec perdat curiam nec socnam suam, quamdiu non difforciauerit rectum.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 576 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: the men of the lord of the court who are accused
die Kläger (oder bessere: [Verklagte] ad sat. habeantur oder habeat)
the plaintiffs (or read: [the accused] ad sat. habeantur or habeat)
satisfaccioni habeantur Rs, nämlich Beklagte durch deren Gerichtsherrn zur Genugtuung, wie ich vorschlug. Vgl. Gl Justizweigerung 4—uel{18}—57, 6 crau.{24} gebessert aus curu. Rs
satisfaccioni habeantur Rs, that is, the accused [are to be held] to satisfaction by their lord of the court, as I proposed. Cf. Gl Justizweigerung 4—uel{18}—57, 6 crau.{24} corrected from curu. Rs

div.ab: If anyone is to do right in his court concerning his men, let those who are impleaded be named to him; and let them [the plaintiffs] have satisfaction at a proper term; and let him not lose his court or his soke, so long as he has not deforced right.
